free_tier.stated: 20 GB automatic on account creation, with an increase process that is explicitly designed to succeed: 'if needed, request reasonable quota increase … all reasonable requests will be approved subject to system capacity limitations'. No absolute ceiling is published. The only stated limit is capacity. So the honest number is 20 GB default with an unbounded-by-documentation increase path, and any 500 GB+ claim depends on a human granting it. A second lever: on publish, the storage is transferred off the author's quota — . 'CUAHSI will assume the burden of storage for published resources'. So publishing frees the quota for reuse.

egress.terms: Free and anonymous. Verified: the resource data endpoint serves a bagit zip to a logged-out client with no credentials.

tooling: HS REST API at /hsapi/ returns JSON from /hsapi/resource/?format=json without authentication. A documented external storage mount feature allows registering resources whose objects reside in external S3 or iRODS storage, functioning as a metadata and DOI catalog layer.
chaining: Resources are unlimited; quota is per-user and transferable ('The quota holder … can be transferred between owner[s]'). Publishing moves the bytes off your quota onto CUAHSI's, then the freed 20 GB is reusable — so the pattern is publish-then-refill, repeated. Community/group resources can pool several members' quotas.

extras.agent_focus: 2026-era research-data and data-marketplace platforms, deliberately judged on the BINDING constraint (does a person with only an email get past the write gate?) rather than on the marketing quota. Coverage: IEEE DataPort (the wave-7 discovery this slot confirms and extends), Mozilla Data Collective (2025 launch, the only new ≥100 GB-per-file free host found), Source Cooperative re-probed at the byte level, the French national Dataverse (Recherche Data Gouv) as the one genuinely EU-funded space with a self-serve email account, plus the 2026 data-marketplace entrants (Snowflake, Databricks Free Edition, data.world, Datarade, Tableland, Spice.ai, DataChain), the EU Data Spaces (Gaia-X / Catena-X / EOSC EU Node / DICE) and ResearchGate/Academia.edu data upload. Two structural results dominate: (a) the 'data marketplace' category is uniformly not storage — they are catalogues, and every one of them fails on per-object size by two to three orders of magnitude; (b) the EU Data Spaces are real and large but gated on eduGAIN/eIDAS identity, so they are closed on identity exactly like CSC Allas and LUMI-O before them.
